dialogue.text: [warm, storytelling] The reason is simple. If the florist gets annoyed, she can take her hundred and sixty thousand dollars across the street tomorrow. Jess can't take her money anywhere, because with the fee on top, she owes this bank ninety-four dollars.
She's a flight risk. You're a sure thing.
[serious, building tension] So if the people at the top get their fees back, who's paying for all that pampering? Gloria turns her screen toward Jess.
Pick any hundred accounts. How many do you think pay most of the overdraft fees?

[serious, building tension] The real answer is nine accounts out of a hundred. When the government's consumer watchdog dug through the data, it found that those nine paid almost eighty percent of all overdraft and bounced-check fees. Most of them are people who come up a few days short, month after month.
